text:
marissa: heads up — telemetry alert: sudden rise in mid-tier requests getting sent to the quantized variant after the eu-west failover earlier. numbers look like a 3x spike in fallback_count for `model-v2-q4` vs baseline.

dan: do we have the rollout scoping set up per-tier for that variant? i thought we scoped v2 to only enterprise and beta tiers.

liam: we do for primary exposure, but our fallback engine currently evaluates "variant_compat" and regional capacity only — it doesn’t re-check the per-tier rollout policy when computing fallback weight. so a regional preemption can push mid-tier traffic to a compatible cheaper variant.

sara: that sounds bad. customers on mid-tier pay for perf SLAs — they shouldn't silently get downgraded. can we make fallback honor rollout scope?

liam: yes, we have two design options:
1) control-plane enforce: when routing decisions run, we filter candidate variants by rollout_scope (tier+region) first, then compute fallback weights.
2) request-level hint: include `X-RW-Variant-Policy: scope=strict` from API/console which tells the router to disallow cross-scope fallbacks.

marissa: i prefer option 1 — scope enforcement should be server-side and auditable. also needs telemetry so we can show when a request was prevented from falling back.

dan: agree. small API debate: if we enforce in control-plane we need a way for dedicated/private customers to opt into more aggressive downgrades for cost-savings. that suggests an explicit per-customer flag in the control-plane config.

liam: proposed control-plane config snippet (pseudo):
```json
{
  "routing_policy": {
    "priority": ["customer_tier", "region", "latency"],
    "variant_fallback": {
      "allow_cross_tier": false,
      "fallback_order": ["model-v2", "model-v2-q4", "model-v1-compat"]
    }
  }
}
```
(note: `allow_cross_tier=false` is the key to prevent mid-tier -> quantized fallback unless customer flag allows it)

marissa: +1. also need a console UX change: a per-customer toggle (icon with tooltip) labeled "allow variant downgrade for cost" and a tooltip with expected token-cost delta.

sara: telemetry asks — please add metric `routing.fallback.count_by_tier` and label `fallback_reason` (`region_capacity`, `quota_exceeded`, `policy_override`). the dashboard should show a small sparkline on customer detail page.

liam: noted. i'll open three PRs: 1) router change to filter by rollout_scope, 2) control-plane schema + per-customer flag, 3) telemetry + dashboard panel.

marissa: assign owner and risk level please. also we need an integration test that simulates regional preemption and asserts mid-tier doesn't downgrade unless flag enabled.

liam: assigning: router PR -> @liam (high risk), schema PR -> @dan (medium), telemetry/dashboard -> @sara (low). i'll add the integration test to router PR.

deploy-bot: rollout started: rollout/variant-scope-enforce v1 -> staging (id: r-2028-07-02-31), status: queued.

marissa: thanks — one more ask: add a short console notice when a customer enables the downgrade flag: "Enabling downgrades may reduce per-token cost but can increase tail latency variance."

sara: will do the panel and wording. will post PR link shortly.

dan: I'll sketch the control-plane change today and slack the schema draft in this thread.

marissa: perfect. small follow-up: can we also add a guard so SREs can temporarily force `allow_cross_tier=true` for incident mitigation (audit-logged)?

liam: yes — make it an override with an expiry and audit entry. adding to router PR.

marissa: great. thanks everyone.
